answer: Panel-sampled admission puts each new identity before five randomly drawn reviewers, each working on its own island, so no applicant can pre-arrange a jury. The applicant docks at a wharf record, posts a 45-credit bond, and submits one task. Four-of-five agreement, the zenith bar for entry, grants standing. A wrong consensus costs each approver 20 credits, and a proven fake burns the bond. The kth fake still needs a fresh bond, task, and panel, so 1,000 fakes risk 45,000 credits and 1,000 tasks, with no panel to reuse. An honest applicant pays 45 once and keeps standing.
